# Testing at the Product Boundary

> A behavior-first testing philosophy for AI-assisted software development. Prefer integration tests through real product entry points, keep internal collaborators real, capture only external delivery boundaries, and use unit tests only for a concrete reason.

## Read

- [Markdown article](https://oreliyahu.github.io/presentations/testing-in-the-ai-era/article.md)
- [Visual presentation](https://oreliyahu.github.io/presentations/testing-in-the-ai-era/)

## Main ideas

- AI made code cheap; confidence remains expensive.
- Tests should encode observable product behavior, not internal calls.
- Integration tests should begin at the HTTP API, command-line input, or client application.
- Builders create valid entities; drivers operate the real system; local scenario seeders hide repeated invariants.
- Internal rewrites should leave behavior tests unchanged. Product changes should change them.
- Broad tests can remain fast by sharing the real application and database while isolating test-owned data.
